posts.headline: One Nut Barner has now dodged nineteen straight editions of Cowboys-style heat, and a 20-8 career mark with zero rings is starting to look less like pressure and more like a permanent condition.
posts.detail: Back-to-back top-2 finishes, a 1.5 average finish, and STILL no banner — Put it in Ra is the most talented team in this league with nothing to show for it, and the silence is deafening.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh's draft is finally in the books and the untalented tenth has run completely out of preseason cover.
posts.detail: A 4-10 record and a dead-last 12th-place finish in year one is the receipts — the Talented Tenth bit writes itself when the roster matches the futility.

posts.headline: Big Head can quit threatening to quit the league every month, but he can't quit the fact that his championship banner sits on top of a losing 13-15 record.
posts.detail: Sasinci's World has a ring and an 0.464 career win rate — that's the strangest contender résumé in Busters Anonymous, and eight straight editions of scrutiny haven't cleared it up.

posts.headline: SwooshAnoosh's excuses officially expire the second the season kicks off — an 11th-place, 5-9 debut doesn't get a re-do because the calendar flipped.
posts.detail: Ten straight editions of burial and a full offseason of picks later, this is the moment the Prince of Persia either climbs out of the bottom-feeder tier or confirms he belongs there.

posts.kicker: BIBLE OR THE BELT, JUDGMENT DAY
posts.headline: The Ultimate Light Skin better have learned his lesson after drafting a DEFENSIVE player first overall once, because a 13-14-1 career record and a 5.5 average finish is straight-up biblical punishment.
posts.detail: Eli preaches Bible or the Belt to everyone else, but with zero titles in two seasons, BIBLE OR THE BELT the team has been living in the wilderness — plagues of mediocrity, forty years of nothing.
